At `z=a`, `z=b`, or `z=c` the quadruple repeats a point, so `[a,b;c,z]` is outside the stated domain; the set-builder does not type-check on all quantified `z` and does not license the defining triple itself to lie on `C(a,b,c)`.

So the claimed equivalence excludes a map that the definition's first sentence includes.

With the ordinary meaning of `P(z)/Q(z)`, no such quotient is `\infty` for every finite `z`, so the theorem omits this meromorphic sphere map.
